concept: Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials
summary: Source-anchored research for Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Parkin is an E3 ligase that functions together with the ubiquitin kinase PINK1 to flag damaged mitochondria for removal via a selective form of autophagy known as mitophagy. (high confidence)
Mutations in the Parkin and PINK1 proteins are the most common form of autosomal recessive PD. (high confidence)

pS65-Ubiquitin (pUb) is a PINK1 substrate, and a Michael J. Fox Foundation grant page says the differential effectiveness of PINK1 activator compounds will be determined by analyzing specific biomarkers. (medium confidence)
The buntanetap Phase 3 study in early PD did not meet its primary endpoint of MDS-UPDRS Part II, according to the published paper and Alzforum. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

The original primary endpoint of the buntanetap early-PD study was the sum of MDS-UPDRS Part II and Part III; the paper and the sponsor release state it was changed to MDS-UPDRS Part II per FDA guidance or feedback. (high confidence)

In its press release the sponsor reported statistical improvement in MDS-UPDRS Part II, Part III, Part II+III and Total scores in Parkinson’s patients with a >3-year diagnosis; Fierce Biotech reports this subgroup as 158 participants. (medium confidence)

The registry record for NCT07174310 lists an estimated enrollment of 900 and a primary outcome of time to confirmed motor progression event on MDS-UPDRS Part III score, with a time frame of up to at least Week 104. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

VacSYn (NCT06015841) is a Phase 2 trial of the active anti-alpha-synuclein immunotherapy ACI-7104.056; AC Immune states Part 1 randomized 34 patients 3:1 to ACI-7104.056 or placebo. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

The EJS ACT-PD consortium describes a multi-arm, multi-stage (MAMS) platform trial design that will start with one placebo and three treatment arms, each with 400 participants, with a primary endpoint at 3 years powered to detect a 30% reduction in rate of progression of MDS-UPDRS Part I and II summed scores, with ineffective arms closed. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-22)

The ASPro-PD protocol gives the primary outcome as the combined score of parts I, II, and III of the MDS-UPDRS, whereas the Cure Parkinson's trial page says the MDS-UPDRS Part III rating scale will be used to measure changes in motor symptoms. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

In MOVES-PD part 2, 221 participants were randomly assigned to venglustat (n=110) or placebo (n=111), and the absolute difference between groups in the MDS-UPDRS parts II and III combined score was 2·58 (95% CI -1·10 to 6·27; p=0·17). (low confidence)

The authors of the phase 2 lixisenatide trial report that at 12 months MDS-UPDRS part III scores had changed by -0.04 points with lixisenatide and 3.04 points with placebo (difference, 3.08; 95% confidence interval, 0.86 to 5.30; P = 0.007). (high confidence)

A 2017 phase II exenatide trial of 62 patients treated for 48 weeks reported a mean 3.5-point advantage over placebo in off-medication MDS-UPDRS part III scores, assessed at 60 weeks. (medium confidence)
The LUMA primary endpoint was time to confirmed worsening in the MDS-UPDRS Parts II and III combined score. (high confidence)

The REASON authors report adverse events in 64.5% (20/31) of part A participants and 84.8% (28/33) of part B participants, mainly mild to moderate and not dose limiting, with no serious adverse events related to BIIB094. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

REASON participant numbers differ by source: the paper abstract reports 40 participants in part A and 42 in part B, while the registry record NCT03976349 lists 62 actual enrollment. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

ClinicalTrials.gov lists Parts 1-4 of the MTX325 study as complete, and Mission reports that in a completed Phase 1a SAD/MAD study in healthy volunteers, MTX325 demonstrated high CNS penetration, while a PET study confirmed distribution into brain parenchyma. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

Alzforum states the company did not report on the primary endpoint in the group as a whole when it announced results on July 2, 2024; Fierce Biotech says the release skirted the question of whether buntanetap moved the needle on the main goal. (high confidence)

In the phase 1b study of anle138b in PD (NCT04685265), the conference abstract reports 70 participants were enrolled in cohorts A-E and that anle138b was safe and well tolerated when administered 7-28 days; the registry lists 70 actual participants. (medium confidence)

Ahlskog and Uitti argue that interpretation of the ADAGIO rasagiline delayed-start trials is problematic because of divergent results with the 2 symptomatically beneficial doses and variability in UPDRS scores with active rasagiline that was twice the magnitude of the major finding. (low confidence)

Mission states that its MTX325-101 Phase 1b study is designed to establish clinical proof-of-mechanism using a wide range of biomarkers and imaging measures, and the registry's official title for NCT07630545 includes assessing CNS penetration, biodistribution, and biomarkers. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

The buntanetap Phase 3 study in early PD (registry NCT05357989) enrolled 523 participants in a 6-month, randomized, double-blind, dose-ranging design testing 10 mg and 20 mg buntanetap against placebo. (high confidence)

A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1a trial of anle138b in healthy volunteers enrolled 68 participants and reported exposure levels above the fully effective exposure in the MI2 mouse Parkinson model at multiple doses of 200 mg. (low confidence)

Alzforum reports that in January 2026 a Phase 2/3 study began to enroll 500 Parkinson’s patients for a three-year, open-label safety study of 30 mg daily buntanetap. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-10)

PADOVA is a Phase 2b, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study in which individuals with early-stage PD on stable symptomatic monotherapy (levodopa or MAO-Bi) receive intravenous prasinezumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks. (medium confidence)

Roche reports that in a pre-specified analysis the effect of prasinezumab in PADOVA was more pronounced in the population treated with levodopa (75% of participants), with HR=0.79 and a nominal p=0.0431. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-06-16)

AC Immune reports that in the interim Phase 2 VacSYn analysis ACI-7104.056 induced a 100% responder rate, and at week 76 serum antibody titers were over 500-fold higher than in the placebo group. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-12-11)

The Mullin et al. ambroxol trial in PD was a single-center open-label noncontrolled clinical trial in which 18 patients completed the study, with escalating oral ambroxol up to 1.26 g per day. (medium confidence)
In the open-label Mullin trial, the authors report that CSF GCase activity decreased by 19% while CSF α-synuclein concentration increased by 13%. (low confidence)

The ASPro-PD protocol reports that approximately 10–15% of individuals with PD carry a GBA1 variant, and a Movement Disorders review reports 5%–10% in Asian and approximately 10%–15% in European populations. (medium confidence)

Bial's ACTIVATE phase 2 study was announced as testing two fixed-dose levels of BIA 28-6156 (10mg and 60mg/day), an allosteric activator of GCase, against placebo, with clinical progression assessed for up to 78 weeks of double-blind treatment. (medium confidence)

Exenatide-PD3 was a phase 3, multicentre, double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled trial at six research hospitals in the UK that randomly assigned 194 participants to extended-release exenatide 2 mg once per week over 96 weeks or placebo. (high confidence)

In the phase 2 lixisenatide trial, the authors report nausea in 46% and vomiting in 13% of participants receiving lixisenatide, and MJFF adds that more than a third needed a reduced dose. (medium confidence)
NeurologyLive, reporting a late-breaking conference presentation, gives the LUMA primary-endpoint hazard ratio as 1.04 (95% CI, 0.85-1.28; P =.4538). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-05)

Biogen and Denali report exploratory LUMA biomarker results of >90% kinase inhibition of peripheral LRRK2 (phosphoserine 935) and, in a CSF sub-study, up to approximately 30% reduction in phosphorylated Rab10. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-21)

The REASON authors report that cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) LRRK2 and phosphorylated Rab10 levels were lowered by up to 59% and up to 50%, respectively, irrespective of LRRK2 variant status after intrathecal BIIB094. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)
In the NT-0796 phase 1b study, 10 subjects with PD received 150 mg open-label NT-0796 every 12 h for 28 days. (medium confidence)

UCB announced on 16 December 2024 that ORCHESTRA, a study of minzasolmin, an oral small-molecule alpha-synuclein misfolding inhibitor, did not meet its primary and secondary clinical endpoints in early Parkinson’s disease. (high confidence)
The Lancet's Department of Error notice states that the appendix of the PADOVA article has been corrected as of July 2, 2026. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-02)

Recent reviews state that no disease-modifying therapy for Parkinson's disease has been established: one says there are currently no disease-modifying therapies (DMTs), and a trial-pipeline analysis says there are still no treatments to modify the course of the disease. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-17)

A ClinicalTrials.gov-based analysis of Parkinson's disease drug trials registered between 2015–2024 reports 444 trials, of which 42% were in Phase 1, 46% in Phase 2 and 12% in Phase 3, with 63% evaluating symptomatic therapies and 37% testing disease-modifying therapies. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-26)

Mari and Mestre describe a “valley of death” in Parkinson's disease modification populated by failures such as the various NET-PD trials, the ADAGIO trial, the more recent α-Synuclein immunotherapy trials and the Ven-glustat trial. (low confidence)

Isradipine evidence is split: the STEADY-PD III report concluded that isradipine did not slow clinical progression, while a re-analysis of STEADY-PD II data reports significantly smaller total and part 3 UPDRS scores with 10 mg/day ER isradipine than placebo at trial end, with post hoc adjustment for symptomatic therapy diminishing the statistical significance. (medium confidence)

In FAIRPARK-II (NCT02655315), a phase 2 trial in participants with newly diagnosed Parkinson's disease who had never received levodopa, the authors report that the mean MDS-UPDRS total score worsened by 15.6 points with deferiprone and 6.3 points with placebo (difference, 9.3 points; 95% confidence interval, 6.3 to 12.2; P<0.001) at 36 weeks, and the trial team's statement likewise reports greater deterioration with deferiprone than with placebo. (high confidence)

The FAIRPARK-II trial team's statement says that 4 other independent deferiprone trials involving about 240 people with Parkinson's disease, in which all participants were already receiving dopamine replacement drugs, observed no worsening of symptoms, and that this difference is probably where the explanation for the conflicting results lies. (low confidence)

Reviewers report that disease-modification trials in neurodegenerative disorders have struggled to separate symptomatic effects of putative agents from disease modification, and that documenting a disease-modifying effect is difficult for a Parkinson's disease drug with symptomatic benefit. (high confidence)
A systematic review that searched 1980–2015 included 128 RCTs (84 in AD, 44 in PD) and concluded that none of the included studies convincingly demonstrated disease-modification. (low confidence)

A PRISMA-compliant review of phase II and III disease-modifying trials (2020-2025) with at least one target-engagement biomarker included 26 trials (PD=19, MSA=4, DLB=3); the authors report that only 8/26 studies demonstrated both target engagement and statistically significant clinical benefit and that nine trials showed target engagement without clinical benefit. (low confidence)

Authors of two reviews attribute the lack of success of disease-modification trials to factors including the complexity of Parkinson's disease, variability between patients and biomarkers for stratification, advanced pathology at diagnosis, insensitive clinical endpoints and scales, and intervention timing in advanced stages of neurodegeneration. (medium confidence)
In the open-label noncontrolled Mullin trial, scores on part 3 of the Movement Disorders Society Unified Parkinson Disease Rating Scale decreased (ie, improved) by 6.8 points. (medium confidence)

In a 52-week phase 2 randomised trial of ambroxol in Parkinson disease dementia, 55 patients were randomised and the authors report no evidence to suggest differences between groups on primary or secondary outcomes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-08-01)

Secondary reports on the Parkinson disease dementia ambroxol trial note that the sample size for GBA1 variant carriers was too small to say for certain that apparent improvements were real, and they list recruiting more GBA1 carriers for future studies. (medium confidence)

The registry record for NCT07011771, the Capsida Biotherapeutics Phase 1/2 trial of CAP-003 gene therapy in GBA1 associated Parkinson's disease, lists the status as WITHDRAWN, with the stated reason that a protocol stopping rule was met for a separate trial of a different disease state and therapy using similar technology. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

The authors of the phase 3 exenatide trial state that they found no evidence to support exenatide as a disease-modifying treatment for people with Parkinson's disease, and that exenatide was safe and well tolerated. (high confidence) (verified as of 2025-02-04)

A Lancet Expression of Concern now qualifies the published exenatide disease-modification trial: the trial authors report no evidence of benefit, while the Lancet notice says the impact of regulatory inspection findings on the study data and reported conclusions is still being assessed. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

A phase 2, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of daily subcutaneous lixisenatide or placebo for 12 months, followed by a 2-month washout period, enrolled 156 participants diagnosed with Parkinson's disease less than 3 years earlier. (high confidence)

The stated repurposing rationale for GLP-1 receptor agonists in Parkinson's disease is neurotrophic or neuroprotective effects in preclinical models, plus epidemiological studies and small randomised trials suggesting possible benefit. (high confidence)

The authors of the phase 3 exenatide trial write that agents with better target engagement, or studies in specific subgroups of patients, are needed to establish whether GLP-1 receptor agonists have any support in Parkinson's disease, and MJFF likewise says carefully controlled study populations could reveal groups who respond better. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-02-04)
Biogen and Denali report that the Phase 2b LUMA study of BIIB122 in early-stage Parkinson’s disease did not meet its primary or secondary endpoints. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-21)

LUMA included individuals with early-stage Parkinson’s disease with or without a pathogenic LRRK2 variant, and MJFF describes the trial as largely including people without known genetic mutations. (high confidence)

Based on the LUMA results, Biogen and Denali state they will discontinue further development of BIIB122 in idiopathic Parkinson’s disease, while Denali continues the Phase 2a BEACON study in carriers of a pathogenic LRRK2 variant. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-21)

BEACON is registered as a Phase 2a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of BIIB122 in LRRK2-associated Parkinson's disease whose primary outcome is the incidence of TEAEs and SAEs over a 12-week double-blind period. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

Mission Therapeutics announced that the first patient has been dosed in its Phase 1b proof-of-mechanism study of MTX325, and ClinicalTrials.gov lists Part 5 (multiple doses in patients with Parkinson's Disease) as in progress. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

A news report on a conference presentation says that in Roche's selnoflast study in Parkinson's disease, the inflammasome-driven cytokine response in lipopolysaccharide-treated blood samples was down by about 90 percent from study start and IL-18 in cerebrospinal fluid had fallen by about 30 percent on day 28, with no differences in the placebo group. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-27)

Dapansutrile, described as having a highly specific effect on the NLRP3 inflammasome, is in a Phase 2 trial in Parkinson's disease registered as NCT07157735 with status RECRUITING and an estimated 36 participants. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

ORCHESTRA (NCT04658186) was a Phase 2a, randomised, placebo-controlled, 18-month study of oral minzasolmin at 180mg/day or 360mg/day versus placebo in early-stage Parkinson’s disease, with primary endpoint progression in the MDS-UPDRS Parts I–III sum score. (high confidence)

In PADOVA, the primary endpoint of time to confirmed motor progression was not met: Roche reports HR=0.84 and p=0.0657, and the Lancet paper reports a non-significant delay in motor progression with prasinezumab versus placebo. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-30)

SURE-PD3 (NCT02642393), a phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of inosine in early Parkinson's disease, randomized 298 participants and closed early after a prespecified interim futility analysis; the authors report MDS-UPDRS progression of 11.1 points per year with inosine versus 9.9 with placebo (P = .18). (high confidence)

STEADY-PD III (NCT02168842), a phase 3 trial that randomized 336 patients with early Parkinson's disease to isradipine 5 mg twice daily or placebo for 36 months, reported adjusted least-squares mean changes in total UPDRS of 2.99 versus 3.26 points (treatment effect —0.27; P = 0.85), and its authors conclude that isradipine did not slow clinical progression. (high confidence)

In the SPARK phase 2 trial (NCT03318523) of cinpanemab in early Parkinson's disease, the authors report the trial was stopped after the week 72 interim analysis owing to lack of efficacy, with a week 52 change in MDS-UPDRS of 10.8 points in the control group versus 10.5, 11.3 and 10.9 points in the 250-mg, 1250-mg and 3500-mg groups. (medium confidence)

MOVES-PD, which evaluated the glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor venglustat, was described as unsuccessful in a Movement Disorders review, and its authors report that venglustat showed no beneficial treatment effect compared with placebo. (medium confidence)

MJFF states that trials of other drugs in the same class, including NLY01 and PT320, reported no meaningful effect, and MedPage Today reports that the pegylated exenatide analogue NLY01 found no overall benefit compared with placebo but suggested benefits in younger patients. (low confidence)

NeurologyLive reports that treatment-emergent adverse events led to study drug withdrawal in 11.2% of BIIB122/DNL151-treated LUMA participants versus 4.6% of placebo-treated participants. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-05)

LIGHTHOUSE (NCT05418673), a Phase 3 study of BIIB122/DNL151 in participants with Parkinson's disease and pathogenic LRRK2 variants, is registered as TERMINATED with the reason Sponsor Decision and 7 actual participants; NeurologyLive attributes the June 2023 termination to complexity and a projected completion date of 2031 rather than any safety or efficacy concern. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

A news report on a conference presentation says selnoflast motor outcomes were exploratory: MDS-UPDRS Part III improved by two to three points in the selnoflast group versus worsening by a point or less on placebo, and average differences were small and not statistically significant. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-27)

A review reports that in sargramostim, a recombinant GMCSF, undergoing extended phase 1 testing, initial results with 8 weeks of treatment in 20 patients with PD showed increased numbers and suppressive function of peripheral T regulatory cells and a modest reduction in UPDRS part III scores versus the placebo arm. (low confidence)

Buntanetap, formerly Posiphen, is described as a small molecule that inhibits translation of aggregation-prone proteins including APP, tau and α-synuclein; Alzforum notes Posiphen reportedly blocks translation of α-synuclein mRNA. (high confidence)

The paper reports that buntanetap improved cognition in a post-hoc analysis, with nominally statistically significant dose-dependent benefits in amyloid-positive PD patients with mild cognitive impairment and mild dementia; Alzforum notes MMSE was not listed as a study outcome. (high confidence)

Two sources give different sizes for the buntanetap subgroup with MMSE scores of 20 to 28: Alzforum reports 173 patients and the paper reports 182 participants. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

UCB states it has initiated measures to terminate the extension phase of the minzasolmin program, and Alzforum and the Michael J. Fox Foundation state that the companies terminated the long-term extension or do not plan to continue testing. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

The Michael J. Fox Foundation interview states the ORCHESTRA trial was launched before the alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay existed, so it is not known for sure that enrolled participants had the misfolded alpha-synuclein pathology the drug targeted. (low confidence)

The primary outcomes registered for the anle138b phase 1b study (NCT04685265) are safety measures such as incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, and the conference abstract states efficacy trials in patients with synucleinopathies are planned. (medium confidence)
The Lancet PADOVA paper describes prasinezumab as a humanised monoclonal antibody that binds the C-terminus of aggregated forms of α-synuclein. (medium confidence)

The Lancet paper's interpretation states that although PADOVA did not meet the primary endpoint, prespecified exploratory evidence suggests clinical activity of prasinezumab, supporting continued investigation in the phase 3 PARAISO trial (NCT07174310). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-30)

Roche announced its decision to proceed with Phase III development of prasinezumab, and a Michael J. Fox Foundation news page described the drug as moving into the Phase III stage of clinical trials. (high confidence) (verified as of 2025-06-17)

The registry record lists NCT07174310 (PARAISO) with phase PHASE3, overall status RECRUITING, an ACTUAL start date of 2025-11-24 and an ESTIMATED primary completion date of 2029-06-30. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

A Nature Medicine analysis compared the PASADENA open-label extension with an external comparator cohort from the PPMI observational study; the authors describe it as an exploratory analysis that requires confirmation in future studies. (high confidence)

In the phase 2 SPARK trial of the anti-α-synuclein antibody cinpanemab, the authors report the trial was stopped after the week 72 interim analysis owing to lack of efficacy, with 357 participants enrolled. (medium confidence)

The registry record lists NCT06015841 with overall status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, an ESTIMATED enrollment of 150 and an ESTIMATED primary completion date of 2028-06. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

AC Immune reports that total CSF a-syn levels stabilized in the ACI-7104.056 arm while decreasing in the placebo group (post-hoc analysis p=0.018), and describes clinical measures of motor symptoms as a trend for stabilization. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-12-11)

In an interview published by the Michael J. Fox Foundation, Kenneth Marek of the Institute for Neurodegenerative Disorders said results from the PADOVA Phase II study were far less clear, and potentially encouraging, though more research is needed. (low confidence)
The STEADY-PD III authors state that the isradipine dose may have been insufficient to engage the target calcium channels associated with neuroprotective effects. (low confidence)
Mullin et al. report that ambroxol was detected in cerebrospinal fluid, with a 156-ng/mL increase in the level of ambroxol in CSF between days 0 and 186. (medium confidence)

The ASPro-PD protocol describes a phase 3, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of high-dose ambroxol that will enrol 330 PD patients with confirmed GBA1 status. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)
ASPro-PD, a phase 3 ambroxol trial, was initiated in 2025. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

A Movement Disorders review reports that in one analysis of 395 PD patients without GBA1 variants, approximately one‐third showed decreased GCase activity comparable with that observed in GBA1 variant carriers. (medium confidence)

Bial reports that the phase 2b ACTIVATE study of BIA 28-6156 (pariceract) in patients with a pathogenic GBA1 variant did not meet its primary, nor the key secondary, efficacy endpoint, and that Bial decided to discontinue further development of BIA 28-6156 for this indication. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-12)

The authors of the exenatide trial report that at 96 weeks MDS-UPDRS III OFF-medication scores, the primary outcome, worsened by a mean of 5.7 points with exenatide and 4.5 points with placebo. (high confidence) (verified as of 2025-02-06)

The Lancet notice says that on May 18, 2026 it was made aware of regulatory inspection findings at King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, one of the trial sites, which identified department-wide concerns relating to trial conduct, oversight, and governance, including findings classified by regulators as critical and major. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

In the phase 2 lixisenatide trial the authors report that other results for the secondary end points did not differ substantially between groups, and MJFF notes that patient-reported secondary measures did not confirm the slowing seen on motor measures. (medium confidence)

As of the registry record's last update on 2026-05-06, the registry lists NCT04232969, the exenatide phase PHASE3 trial, as COMPLETED, with a start date of 2020-01-20 and 194 actual participants. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)
LUMA participant numbers differ by source: Biogen and Denali cite 648 people, while the registry record NCT05348785 lists 650 actual enrollment. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)
Biogen and Denali state that BIIB122 was generally well tolerated with an acceptable safety profile in LUMA. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-21)

The registry record for BEACON (NCT06602193) lists the study as ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING with an estimated primary completion of 2027-03, and Biogen and Denali state that BEACON data are anticipated in the first half of 2027. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

The REASON authors describe BIIB094 (ION859) as an antisense oligonucleotide that targets LRRK2 mRNA for degradation; REASON (NCT03976349) was a first-in-human randomized phase 1 study of intrathecal BIIB094 in patients with PD. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

A Science Translational Medicine summary states that several different LRRK2 inhibitors induced on-target histopathological changes in the lungs of nonhuman primates that were reversible after drug withdrawal and had no effect on pulmonary function; Alzforum describes three inhibitors tested at least over a period of two weeks. (high confidence)
USP30, a deubiquitinase localized to mitochondria, antagonizes mitophagy driven by the ubiquitin ligase parkin and the protein kinase PINK1. (high confidence)

One study reports that knockdown of USP30 rescues the defective mitophagy caused by pathogenic mutations in parkin, and another reports that USP30 inhibition promoted mitophagy in PARK2 KO neurons. (medium confidence)

In an αSyn-induced model, Usp30 knockout mice are reported to show protection against behavioral deficits, increased mitophagy, decreased phospho-S129 αSyn, and attenuation of SN dopaminergic neuronal loss. (medium confidence)
The authors report that the observations in knockout mice were recapitulated with MTX115325, a potent, selective, brain-penetrant USP30 inhibitor. (medium confidence)

Reports differ on MTK458: a preprint describes a brain penetrant small molecule that binds to PINK1 and stabilizes its active complex, while Science Advances authors report that MTK458 induces mild mitochondrial stress through PINK1/Parkin-independent off-target activities. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

One study reports that basal mammalian mitophagy occurs independently of PINK1, whereas another reports that the age-dependent rise in Drosophila mitophagy is abrogated by PINK1 or parkin deficiency. (medium confidence)
AbbVie acquired Mitokinin in 2023, and AbbVie described Mitokinin's lead compound as a selective PINK1 activator designed to address mitochondrial dysfunction. (medium confidence)
Mission states that recruitment is ongoing for 36 participants with mild to moderate idiopathic PD and that a data readout is anticipated in late 2027. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-15)
Reviews report that α-synuclein can drive NLRP3 inflammasome activation in microglia, and that inflammasome activation releases pro-inflammatory cytokines. (medium confidence)

The authors report that NT-0796 drove reductions in systemic inflammatory markers including high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, fibrinogen and IL-18, and reductions in neuroinflammation within the CNS of subjects with PD. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-27)

The NT-0796 phase 1b study was designed to assess safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and anti-inflammatory effects, and a news report on the work states that motor outcomes were not assessed. (medium confidence)

The VENT-02 Parkinson's study registered as NCT06822517 lists incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) as its primary outcome, and its congress abstract states the primary endpoint is safety. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

Sources differ on the VENT-02 Parkinson's study: the congress abstract and sponsor page describe a Phase 2 program with 30 patients, while registry record NCT06822517 titles it Phase 1b and lists status TERMINATED with 29 enrolled. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

Roche's NCT05924243 study of RO7486967 in early idiopathic PD is registered as a Phase 1b, adaptive, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study with registry status COMPLETED. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

In the AZA-PD randomised, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial (66 randomly assigned: azathioprine n=32, placebo n=34), the primary outcome, change in MDS-UPDRS gait-axial score in the off-state at 12 months, was not met. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

Exploratory analyses in the azathioprine trial suggested effects on immune biomarkers and motor symptoms, but a charity summary calls it a small proof-of-concept trial whose findings need validation in larger trials. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)

Reviews report that minocycline, which reduces microglial activation and shows therapeutic effects in PD animal models, was not progressed to phase 3 and failed to show significant therapeutic efficacy in a Phase II clinical trial. (medium confidence)

A review and a Michael J. Fox Foundation grant summary both frame selecting trial participants by inflammatory phenotype or neuroinflammation-related PD subtype as a route to better trial success. (medium confidence)

A review states that microglia play dual roles in PD, phagocytosing and clearing α-syn aggregates while becoming dysfunctional due to aggregate overload, which drives their transition to a pro-inflammatory phenotype. (low confidence)

narrative.documentConcept: Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap
narrative.text: Covers three alpha-synuclein-directed small molecules: buntanetap (a translation inhibitor), minzasolmin (a misfolding inhibitor) and anle138b (an oligomer modulator). Buntanetap's Phase 3 early-PD study did not meet its primary endpoint per the paper and Alzforum; its cognition findings are post hoc. UCB announced that ORCHESTRA did not meet primary or secondary endpoints and began ending the minzasolmin extension. Anle138b has reported phase 1 safety data, with efficacy trials described as planned.

narrative.documentConcept: Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap
narrative.text: The sponsor release says its results met both primary and secondary endpoints in the specified subgroups, while the paper states the study did not meet its primary endpoint of MDS-UPDRS Part II.

narrative.documentConcept: Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap
narrative.text: Has the planned efficacy trial of anle138b in patients with synucleinopathies reported results?

narrative.documentConcept: Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap
narrative.text: Will prospective trials confirm the post-hoc cognition signal in amyloid-positive PD patients?

narrative.documentConcept: Alpha-synuclein aggregation inhibitors and buntanetap
narrative.text: What do the ORCHESTRA biomarker data, which UCB says showed a preliminary signal, show once analyzed?

narrative.documentConcept: Anti-alpha-synuclein immunotherapy: prasinezumab and vaccines
narrative.text: Prasinezumab binds aggregated alpha-synuclein; its PADOVA trial in early-stage Parkinson's disease did not meet the primary endpoint, and a Phase 3 trial is registered as recruiting. Cinpanemab's SPARK trial was stopped for lack of efficacy. AC Immune's active vaccine ACI-7104.056 is in Phase 2, with sponsor-reported interim biomarker trends.

narrative.documentConcept: Anti-alpha-synuclein immunotherapy: prasinezumab and vaccines
narrative.text: Will the phase 3 PARAISO trial confirm the exploratory PADOVA signal?

narrative.documentConcept: Anti-alpha-synuclein immunotherapy: prasinezumab and vaccines
narrative.text: Will the full VacSYn cohort reproduce the interim biomarker trends?

narrative.documentConcept: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
narrative.text: Recent reviews state that no disease-modifying therapy for Parkinson's disease has been established. This concept collects registry and journal results from trials that did not show disease modification (SURE-PD3 inosine, STEADY-PD III isradipine, FAIRPARK-II deferiprone, SPARK cinpanemab) and, separately, the reasons reviewers give for such failures: symptomatic effects confound disease-modification readouts, delayed-start interpretation is contested, target engagement rarely coincided with clinical benefit in one review, and authors cite patient variability, late-stage pathology and insensitive endpoints. It also notes a post hoc re-analysis that disputes a clean negative reading of isradipine and a proposed multi-arm, multi-stage platform trial.

narrative.documentConcept: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
narrative.text: STEADY-PD III reported that isradipine did not slow clinical progression, while a re-analysis of STEADY-PD II data reports significantly smaller total and part 3 UPDRS scores with 10 mg/day ER isradipine than placebo at trial end, with post hoc adjustment for symptomatic therapy diminishing the statistical significance.

narrative.documentConcept: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
narrative.text: FAIRPARK-II reported worse parkinsonism scores with deferiprone, whereas its trial team notes that 4 other trials in patients already on dopamine replacement drugs saw no worsening.

narrative.documentConcept: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
narrative.text: Rasagiline delayed-start (ADAGIO) outcomes were described as ostensibly positive but obscured by confounding factors intrinsic to the design.

narrative.documentConcept: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
narrative.text: Whether the isradipine signal in the STEADY-PD II re-analysis can be confirmed prospectively.

narrative.documentConcept: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
narrative.text: Whether the FAIRPARK-II worsening depends on the absence of background dopaminergic therapy, as its trial team suggests.

narrative.documentConcept: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
narrative.text: Which biomarkers predict clinical benefit, given that target engagement was frequently demonstrated while clinical benefit rarely followed in a 2026 review.

narrative.documentConcept: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies
narrative.text: GBA1 variants are among the most common genetic risk factors for Parkinson's disease, so drugs aimed at the GCase lysosomal pathway have been tested as possible disease-modifying treatments. An open-label phase 2 ambroxol trial reported CSF penetration. Three later randomised trials reported no benefit on their primary outcomes: venglustat (MOVES-PD), ambroxol in Parkinson disease dementia, and Bial's BIA 28-6156 (ACTIVATE), which Bial then discontinued. The phase 3 ambroxol trial ASPro-PD was initiated in 2025. The registry lists the CAP-003 gene therapy trial as withdrawn. This is a research summary, not clinical advice.

narrative.documentConcept: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies
narrative.text: The ASPro-PD protocol gives the combined MDS-UPDRS parts I, II, and III score as the primary outcome, while the Cure Parkinson's page names the MDS-UPDRS Part III rating scale for motor symptoms.

narrative.documentConcept: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies
narrative.text: Mullin et al. cite reports that ambroxol increases GCase enzyme activity, yet measured a 19% decrease in CSF GCase activity alongside a 35% increase in CSF GCase protein levels.

narrative.documentConcept: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies
narrative.text: What detailed results from the ACTIVATE study (NCT05819359) will Bial present and publish beyond its topline statement?

narrative.documentConcept: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies
narrative.text: Does the ASPro-PD trial use the protocol's combined MDS-UPDRS parts I, II, and III score as its primary outcome?

narrative.documentConcept: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies
narrative.text: Is the CAP-003 gene therapy program continuing in GBA1 Parkinson's disease after the withdrawn NCT07011771 record?

narrative.documentConcept: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD
narrative.text: GLP-1 receptor agonists, developed for diabetes, were tested in Parkinson's disease after preclinical neuroprotection findings and small trials. A single-centre exenatide phase II trial and a phase 2 lixisenatide trial reported motor benefits. The larger exenatide phase 3 trial reported no evidence of disease modification at 96 weeks. The Lancet later issued an Expression of Concern on that paper after a regulatory inspection at a trial site, with an investigation pending. Open issues are phase 2 to phase 3 translation, target engagement and subgroup selection.

narrative.documentConcept: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD
narrative.text: The 2017 exenatide phase II trial reported a motor advantage, whereas the authors of the later phase 3 exenatide trial report no evidence of disease modification.

narrative.documentConcept: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD
narrative.text: Whether the Lancet has updated its Expression of Concern since its online publication on June 22, 2026; the notice says it will be updated as soon as further information is available.

narrative.documentConcept: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD
narrative.text: Whether GLP-1 agents other than exenatide, such as semaglutide, change progression in Parkinson's disease; MedPage Today notes ongoing semaglutide trials.

narrative.documentConcept: LRRK2-targeted therapies: small molecule and antisense
narrative.text: LRRK2 (leucine-rich repeat kinase 2) is a Parkinson's disease target pursued with a small molecule inhibitor, BIIB122 (DNL151), and an intrathecal antisense oligonucleotide, BIIB094 (ION859). Biogen and Denali report that the Phase 2b LUMA study of BIIB122 in early-stage Parkinson’s disease did not meet its primary or secondary endpoints, and that they will discontinue development in idiopathic Parkinson’s disease while Denali continues the Phase 2a BEACON study in carriers of a pathogenic LRRK2 variant. The REASON phase 1 authors report cerebrospinal fluid LRRK2 and phosphorylated Rab10 lowered by up to 59% and up to 50% with BIIB094.

narrative.documentConcept: LRRK2-targeted therapies: small molecule and antisense
narrative.text: Denali's chief medical officer calls LUMA a robust test of LRRK2 inhibition in idiopathic Parkinson’s disease, while a site investigator quoted by MJFF says the mixed population, mostly without LRRK2 mutations, could have affected the results.

narrative.documentConcept: LRRK2-targeted therapies: small molecule and antisense
narrative.text: What BEACON biomarker results will show in carriers of a pathogenic LRRK2 variant (data anticipated in the first half of 2027).

narrative.documentConcept: LRRK2-targeted therapies: small molecule and antisense
narrative.text: Whether the roughly 30% CSF phosphorylated Rab10 reduction in LUMA was sufficient central target engagement.

narrative.documentConcept: LRRK2-targeted therapies: small molecule and antisense
narrative.text: Which peer-reviewed publication will report the full LUMA results, given that the evidence here is a sponsor release, a trade-press report of a conference presentation and registry data?

narrative.documentConcept: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30
narrative.text: PINK1 (a ubiquitin kinase) and parkin (an E3 ligase) flag damaged mitochondria for mitophagy, and mutations in both are linked to autosomal recessive PD. USP30, a mitochondrial deubiquitinase, opposes this pathway. Preclinical mouse and human-neuron studies support USP30 inhibition; Mission Therapeutics reports its USP30 inhibitor MTX325 has reached patients with PD in a Phase 1b study. PINK1 activators such as MTK458 are earlier-stage, and a Science Advances paper reports PINK1/Parkin-independent off-target effects for two activators.

narrative.documentConcept: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30
narrative.text: A mouse-tissue study reports basal mammalian mitophagy independent of PINK1, while a Drosophila study reports PINK1 or parkin deficiency abrogates the age-dependent rise in mitophagy.

narrative.documentConcept: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30
narrative.text: Is Mission Therapeutics' Phase 1b study of MTX325 registered as part of a larger trial, and under which registry identifier?

narrative.documentConcept: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30
narrative.text: Whether the MTK458 preprint has since been peer reviewed is not established; its PMC page says it is a preprint.

narrative.documentConcept: Mitochondrial and mitophagy targets: PINK1, parkin, USP30
narrative.text: What is the registry status of the ABBV-1088 Phase 1 study?

narrative.documentConcept: Neuroinflammation: NLRP3 and microglia targets
narrative.text: NLRP3 inflammasome activation in microglia, which α-synuclein can drive, is a neuroinflammation target in PD. Early NLRP3 inhibitor studies of NT-0796 and selnoflast were short safety and biomarker studies, not efficacy trials. The VENT-02 registry record is TERMINATED. Minocycline and azathioprine did not meet efficacy goals, and a review says selecting participants by inflammatory phenotype could potentially enhance success.

narrative.documentConcept: Neuroinflammation: NLRP3 and microglia targets
narrative.text: Why the VENT-02 study NCT06822517 was terminated beyond the registry reason: Sponsor decision.

narrative.documentConcept: Neuroinflammation: NLRP3 and microglia targets
narrative.text: Whether selnoflast advances to Phase 2 in PD; the news report says Roche did not disclose this.

narrative.documentConcept: Neuroinflammation: NLRP3 and microglia targets
narrative.text: Whether any NLRP3 inhibitor shows motor efficacy in a randomized trial powered for efficacy.
